evidence: Criterion -> requirement map built for all 3 gate, 38 functional, 6 polish and 3 visual criteria against instruction.md and the six notes. Most criteria trace to a stated requirement (e.g. two-space nesting ui.md:15; replace-current moves to following match ui.md:11; focus return ui.md:17; five-second budget and self-rescheduling timers behaviour.md:5; restore idempotency behaviour.md:13; library refresh within about five seconds behaviour.md:11, graded at ten). Indent width, palette, labels, routes, column base and conflict wording are correctly left free. Four criteria assert a detail that no requirement states. (1) scored/polish/judge.toml:59 cw_unsaved_marker: 'read the visible indication of its state: it must say the draft is saved or unchanged', and 'Fails if the app shows no visible saved or unsaved indication'. ui.md:17 only asks to 'Show clearly whether the draft differs from what is saved; that marker goes away after Save and when Undo brings the source back to the saved text', i.e. a marker that is absent when clean. The positive 'Saved' text is what the reference does (solution/app/src/app.tsx:139 'Unsaved changes' : 'Saved'). The same criterion later says 'the unsaved indication must go away', so it is also internally inconsistent about the clean state. (2) scored/functional/judge.toml:47 cw_grapheme_navigation_and_deletion: 'Shift+Arrow must select it whole'. ui.md:5 lists 'arrows, Home and End' for movement and ui.md:7 defines selection only by mouse (click, double click, triple click, drag); grapheme handling is required only to 'move and delete as complete visible characters'. Keyboard range selection is never requested; the reference implements it (custom-editor.js:263,306). It is a common editor convention, so this is the weakest of the four, but qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md 'No hidden requirements' asks that reference defaults be checked against public instructions. (3) scored/functional/judge.toml:245 cw_output_before_failure_kept: marker must be visible 'together with, and above, the visible reason for that run' and 'Fails ... if a marker appears only after its reason'. behaviour.md:3 requires that earlier output 'stays in the console' and behaviour.md:5 only says 'show the reason'; policy.md:3 leaves layout free. Nothing says the stop or time-limit reason is a console entry, or positioned below the output. cw_time_limit_recovery (judge.toml:263) and cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (judge.toml:272) correctly leave the reason's location free, so this criterion is stricter than its siblings. (4) scored/functional/judge.toml:128 cw_undo_restores_caret: 'type a second marker there. Press Undo once: the second marker is removed. Press Undo again: the first marker is removed.' The notes state undo grouping only for paste (ui.md:7), block indent (ui.md:7), a multi-caret typing burst (ui.md:9), Replace all (ui.md:11) and Format (ui.md:15). Single-caret typing grouping is not specified; cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state (judge.toml:353) acknowledges this with 'Undo, pressed once or twice depending on how the app groups typing'. Lesser observations, not counted as defects on their own: cw_same_line_carets (judge.toml:119) requires an undo boundary between a typing burst and the following Backspace; cw_find_forward_backward_wrap (judge.toml:137) requires the current match to be 'a real selection' and assumes the first Next lands on the first occurrence, which an incremental find that already selects the first match on typing would shift by one; cw_error_message_and_line (judge.toml:227) places the error in 'the app console' while behaviour.md:3 does not name the location; cw_history_restore_retry (judge.toml:335) accepts 'the control the app offers for retrying it', which a judge could read as pressing Restore again, a new legitimate request that behaviour.md:13 allows to create a revision. No sign-in criterion exists, so the known false positive does not arise. No configured judge run exists for this candidate; the raw evidence is scripted golden behaviour only, so these are source findings and their effect on a real judge is unmeasured.
counterexample: Conforming app A follows ui.md:17 literally: a dot and the word 'Unsaved' appear only while the draft differs from the saved revision and nothing is shown when it is clean. It satisfies every stated marker rule but fails cw_unsaved_marker at its first step ('must say the draft is saved or unchanged'). Conforming app B implements every listed key and mouse gesture but no Shift+Arrow selection; it moves and deletes the emoji and the decomposed letter whole yet fails cw_grapheme_navigation_and_deletion. Conforming app C shows the Stop and time-limit reason in a status strip above the console pane and keeps the earlier output in the console; the marker is then below the reason and cw_output_before_failure_kept fails. Conforming app D records single-caret typing as one undo step per character (multi-caret bursts, paste, Replace all and Format are atomic as required); it restores the caret correctly on Undo but fails cw_undo_restores_caret because one Undo does not remove a multi-character marker. Weak app in the other direction: none of these four details lets a broken app pass, so the defect is false-fail only.
suggested_fix: Either state the detail publicly or stop grading it. cw_unsaved_marker: accept 'no unsaved marker shown' as the clean state and drop 'must say the draft is saved or unchanged'. cw_grapheme_navigation_and_deletion: remove the Shift+Arrow leg, or add keyboard range selection with Shift+Arrow to ui.md. cw_output_before_failure_kept: require only that the marker is still visible in the console after the reason is shown, without 'above' or 'only after its reason'. cw_undo_restores_caret: say 'press Undo until both markers are removed' (as cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state does), or state in ui.md that a continuous single-caret typing burst is one Undo action. Optionally relax the find and same-line-caret wording noted above.
